segments.arabic: [395] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك بن أنس عن عبد الله بن دينار عن عبد الله بن عمر قال
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik ibn Anas informed us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, who said:

segments.arabic: بينا الناس بقباء في صلاة الصبح إذ جاءهم آت، فقال إن رسول الله ﷺ قد أنزل عليه الليلة قرآن وقد أمر أن يستقبل الكعبة فاستقبلوها وكانت وجوههم إلى الشام فاستداروا إلى الكعبة
segments.english: While the people were at Quba’ in the morning prayer, someone came to them and said: “Qur’an has been revealed to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, tonight, and he has been commanded to face the Ka‘bah, so face it.” Their faces had been towards al-Sham, so they turned towards the Ka‘bah.

notes: The complete chain retains Malik ibn Anas where the historical print shortens the name. The unnamed visitor, morning prayer at Quba, revelation tonight, command and turn from al-Sham to the Kaaba remain. The selected imperative face it is retained; no name, exact date, geographic parenthesis or reconstruction of the rows is supplied.

segments.arabic: [396] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى عن شعبة عن الحكم عن إبراهيم عن علقمة عن عبد الله قال
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Shu‘bah, from al-Hakam, from Ibrahim, from ‘Alqamah, from ‘Abd Allah, who said:

segments.arabic: صلى النبي ﷺ الظهر خمسا فقالوا أزيد في الصلاة قال وما ذاك قالوا صليت خمسا فثنى رجليه وسجد سجدتين
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed five rak‘ahs for Dhuhr. They said: “Has the prayer been increased?” He said: “What is that?” They said: “You prayed five.” He bent his legs and performed two prostrations.

notes: The selected five rakahs at Dhuhr, plural they said, question and response, bent legs and two prostrations remain. No closing salutation or uncertainty from selected 392 is imported. Abd Allah remains unexpanded in the chain.

segments.arabic: [397] حدثنا قتيبة قال: حدثنا إسماعيل بن جعفر عن حميد عن أنس
segments.english: Qutaybah related to us. He said: Isma‘il ibn Ja‘far related to us, from Humayd, from Anas:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ رأى نخامة في القبلة فشق ذلك عليه حتى رؤي في وجهه فقام فحكه بيده، فقال إن أحدكم إذا قام في صلاته فإنه يناجي ربه أو إن ربه بينه وبين القبلة فلا يبزقن أحدكم قبل قبلته ولكن عن يساره أو تحت قدميه ثم أخذ طرف ردائه فبصق فيه ثم رد بعضه على بعض، فقال أو يفعل هكذا
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw phlegm in the direction of the qiblah. It distressed him so much that it could be seen in his face. He stood and scraped it off with his hand. He said: “When one of you stands in his prayer, he is conversing privately with his Lord—or his Lord is between him and the qiblah. So none of you should spit towards his qiblah, but to his left or under his feet.” Then he took the edge of his cloak, spat into it, and folded part of it over the other. He said: “Or he should do this.”

notes: The selected dual under his feet remains, although both inspected prints use singular under his foot. The uncertainty or his Lord is between him and the qiblah remains, without adding a theological interpretation or resolving it into the preceding clause. The distress, standing, hand, cloak and demonstrated alternative are complete.

Phlegm provisionally renders نخامة; source terminology and differing lexical explanations are recorded, without adding an anatomical explanation. The source says in the qiblah; in the direction of the qiblah makes that relation readable without importing an extra mosque-wall phrase from the comparison.

segments.arabic: [398] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن نافع عن عبد الله بن عمر
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ رأى بصاقا في جدار القبلة فحكه ثم أقبل على الناس، فقال إذا كان أحدكم يصلي فلا يبصق قبل وجهه فإن الله قبل وجهه إذا صلى
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw sputum on the qiblah wall and scraped it off. Then he turned towards the people and said: “When one of you is praying, he should not spit in front of his face, for Allah is before his face when he prays.”

notes: The source attribution remains Messenger of Allah. The qiblah wall, scraping, turning towards the people and complete third-person statement remain. The working English renders فإن الله قبل وجهه إذا صلى directly; no explanatory doctrine or modern application is inserted into the quotation.

segments.arabic: [399] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة أم المؤمنين
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘A’ishah, the Mother of the Believers:

segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw mucus, or sputum, or phlegm on the qiblah wall and scraped it off.

segments.arabic: [400] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل قال: أخبرنا إبراهيم بن سعد أخبرنا ابن شهاب عن حميد بن عبد الرحمن أن أبا هريرة وأبا سعيد حدثاه
segments.english: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d informed us; Ibn Shihab informed us, from Humayd ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, that Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa‘id related to him:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ رأى نخامة في جدار المسجد فتناول حصاة فحكها، فقال إذا تنخم أحدكم فلا يتنخمن قبل وجهه ولا عن يمينه وليبصق عن يساره أو تحت قدمه اليسرى
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw phlegm on the wall of the mosque. He took a pebble and scraped it off. He said: “When one of you spits phlegm, he should not spit it in front of his face or to his right. He should spit to his left or under his left foot.”

notes: The dual Abu Hurayrah and Abu Said attribution, one pebble, wall and left foot are preserved. The historical print uses related to us for Ibrahim ibn Sad where the selected and modern print use informed us. The selected two informed-us links remain. Both English comparisons shorten the chain and one has an Abd Huraira spelling; the Arabic names are not changed to match it.

segments.arabic: [401] حدثنا يحيى بن بكير قال: حدثنا الليث عن عقيل عن ابن شهاب عن حميد بن عبد الرحمن أن أبا هريرة وأبا سعيد أخبراه
segments.english: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from Humayd ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, that Abu Hurayrah and Abu Sa‘id informed him:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ رأى نخامة في حائط المسجد فتناول رسول الله ﷺ حصاة فحتها، ثم قال إذا تنخم أحدكم فلا يتنخم قبل وجهه ولا عن يمينه وليبصق عن يساره أو تحت قدمه اليسرى
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw phlegm on the wall of the mosque. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, took a pebble and scraped it off. Then he said: “When one of you spits phlegm, he should not spit it in front of his face or to his right. He should spit to his left or under his left foot.”

segments.arabic: [402] حدثنا حفص بن عمر قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: أخبرني قتادة قال: سمعت أنسا قال: قال النبي ﷺ

segments.arabic: [403] حدثنا آدم قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: حدثنا قتادة قال: سمعت أنس بن مالك قال: قال النبي ﷺ
segments.english: Adam related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: Qatadah related to us. He said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: إن المؤمن إذا كان في الصلاة فإنما يناجي ربه فلا يبزقن بين يديه ولا عن يمينه ولكن عن يساره أو تحت قدمه
segments.english: “When the believer is in prayer, he is conversing privately with his Lord. So he should not spit in front of him or to his right, but to his left or under his foot.”

segments.arabic: [404] حدثنا علي قال: حدثنا سفيان حدثنا الزهري عن حميد بن عبد الرحمن عن أبي سعيد
segments.english: ‘Ali related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us; al-Zuhri related to us, from Humayd ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Sa‘id:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ أبصر نخامة في قبلة المسجد فحكها بحصاة ثم نهى أن يبزق الرجل بين يديه أو عن يمينه ولكن عن يساره أو تحت قدمه اليسرى
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw phlegm in the qiblah of the mosque and scraped it off with a pebble. Then he forbade a man to spit in front of him or to his right, but to his left or under his left foot.

segments.arabic: وعن الزهري سمع حميدا عن أبي سعيد نحوه
segments.english: And from al-Zuhri: he heard Humayd relate from Abu Sa‘id something similar.

notes: The narrator remains Abu Said alone; Abu Hurayrah is not inserted from the nearby dual transmissions. The closing al-Zuhri hearing from Humayd is preserved as another chain, including something similar, although the EPUB omits it and Bewley shortens it. Fath al-Bari identifies this closing phrase as al-Zuhri’s explicit hearing from Humayd. The pebble is singular, unlike a plural English rendering.

segments.arabic: [406] حدثنا إسحاق بن نصر قال: حدثنا عبد الرزاق عن معمر عن همام سمع أبا هريرة عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Ishaq ibn Nasr related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq related to us, from Ma‘mar, from Hammam, who heard Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: إذا قام أحدكم إلى الصلاة فلا يبصق أمامه فإنما يناجي الله ما دام في مصلاه ولا عن يمينه فإن عن يمينه ملكا وليبصق عن يساره أو تحت قدمه فيدفنها
segments.english: “When one of you stands for prayer, he should not spit in front of him, for he is conversing privately with Allah as long as he is in his place of prayer; nor to his right, for there is an angel to his right. He should spit to his left or under his foot and bury it.”

notes: The full chain retains Hammam without importing Ibn Munabbih, and the selected related to us for Abd al-Razzaq; the historical print uses informed us and adds Most High after Allah. Neither difference changes the selected text.

The source’s as long as he is in his place of prayer, angel to his right, unqualified foot and bury it remain. No recording angel or left-foot detail from a comparison is supplied. Commentary about the mosque floor and burial remains outside the hadith wording.

segments.arabic: [407] حدثنا مالك بن إسماعيل قال: حدثنا زهير قال: حدثنا حميد عن أنس
segments.english: Malik ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Zuhayr related to us. He said: Humayd related to us, from Anas:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ رأى نخامة في القبلة فحكها بيده ورؤي منه كراهية أو رؤي كراهيته لذلك وشدته عليه، وقال إن أحدكم إذا قام في صلاته فإنما يناجي ربه أو ربه بينه وبين قبلته فلا يبزقن في قبلته ولكن عن يساره أو تحت قدمه ثم أخذ طرف ردائه فبزق فيه ورد بعضه على بعض قال أو يفعل هكذا
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw phlegm in the direction of the qiblah and scraped it off with his hand. His dislike was seen—or his dislike of it and how distressing it was to him were seen. He said: “When one of you stands in his prayer, he is conversing privately with his Lord—or his Lord is between him and his qiblah. So he should not spit towards his qiblah, but to his left or under his foot.” Then he took the edge of his cloak, spat into it and folded part of it over the other. He said: “Or he should do this.”

notes: Both uncertainty markers remain: the alternate description of visible dislike and the or connecting the statements about prayer. The Khan-family body flattens the first alternative; the working translation follows the selected Arabic and the prints. The complete cloak demonstration and closing alternative remain. The chapter title’s sudden need to spit is not inserted into the report itself.

segments.arabic: [408] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن أبي الزناد عن الأعرج عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: هل ترون قبلتي هاهنا فوالله ما يخفى علي خشوعكم ولا ركوعكم إني لأراكم من وراء ظهري
segments.english: “Do you think my qiblah is here? By Allah, neither your humility nor your bowing is hidden from me. I certainly see you from behind my back.”

notes: The complete selected chain, qiblah question, oath, humility and bowing remain. Humility renders خشوع without substituting prostration from a variant discussed in commentary. The seeing-behind statement is retained without a theological explanation.

He held a race between horses that had not been trained, from al-Thaniyyah to the mosque of Banu Zurayq. ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar was among those who raced them.

notes: Both race routes, trained and untrained horses, the finish and Ibn Umar’s participation remain. The place names are retained without adding distances or a training regimen. segments.arabic: [411] وقال إبراهيم عن عبد العزيز بن صهيب عن أنس رضى الله تعالى عنه قال
segments.english: And Ibrahim said, from ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Suhayb, from Anas, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, who said:

segments.arabic: أتي النبي ﷺ بمال من البحرين، فقال انثروه في المسجد وكان أكثر مال أتي به رسول الله ﷺ
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was brought wealth from Bahrayn. He said: “Spread it out in the mosque.” It was the greatest amount of wealth that had been brought to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

segments.arabic: فخرج رسول الله ﷺ إلى الصلاة ولم يلتفت إليه فلما قضى الصلاة جاء فجلس إليه فما كان يرى أحدا إلا أعطاه
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went out to the prayer without looking towards it. When he had finished the prayer, he came and sat beside it. There was no one he saw without giving him something.

segments.arabic: إذ جاءه العباس، فقال: يا رسول الله أعطني فإني فاديت نفسي وفاديت عقيلا، فقال له رسول الله ﷺ خذ فحثا في ثوبه ثم ذهب يقله فلم يستطع، فقال: يا رسول الله مر بعضهم يرفعه إلي قال لا قال: فارفعه أنت علي قال لا فنثر منه ثم ذهب يقله، فقال: يا رسول الله مر بعضهم يرفعه علي قال لا قال: فارفعه أنت علي قال لا فنثر منه ثم احتمله فألقاه على كاهله ثم انطلق
segments.english: Then al-‘Abbas came to him and said: “Messenger of Allah, give me some, for I paid the ransom for myself and paid the ransom for ‘Aqil.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “Take.” He scooped some into his garment, then tried to lift it but could not. He said: “Messenger of Allah, tell one of them to lift it up to me.” He said: “No.” He said: “Then lift it onto me yourself.” He said: “No.” So he poured out some of it, then tried to lift it. He said: “Messenger of Allah, tell one of them to lift it onto me.” He said: “No.” He said: “Then lift it onto me yourself.” He said: “No.” So he poured out some of it, then lifted it, placed it on his shoulders and went away.

segments.arabic: فما زال رسول الله ﷺ يتبعه بصره حتى خفي علينا عجبا من حرصه فما قام رسول الله ﷺ وثم منها درهم
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, kept following him with his gaze until he disappeared from our sight, astonished at his eagerness. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, did not get up while a dirham of it remained there.

notes: The selected introduction begins And Ibrahim said. It is not changed to a direct related-to-us transmission, nor is Ibn Tahman inserted from the historical print. The original Anas honorific remains. Both complete request-and-refusal cycles, both reductions of the load, our sight and the final dirham remain. The historical print is shorter in the repeated exchange, while the modern print agrees with the selected full sequence.

Eagerness provisionally renders حرص without adding a moral explanation. No amount, tax category, battle date or ransom circumstances from commentary are inserted. Both prints preserve a separate compiler definition of the chapter’s date-bunch term, absent from the digital chapter. It is supplied separately as Arabic chapter material with the dual/plural vowel distinction retained; English is pending.

segments.arabic: [412] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف أخبرنا مالك عن إسحاق بن عبد الله سمع أنسا قال
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us; Malik informed us, from Ishaq ibn ‘Abd Allah, who heard Anas say:

segments.arabic: وجدت النبي ﷺ في المسجد معه ناس فقمت، فقال لي أرسلك أبو طلحة قلت: نعم، فقال لطعام قلت: نعم، فقال لمن معه قوموا فانطلق وانطلقت بين أيديهم
segments.english: I found the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, in the mosque with some people. I stood there. He said to me: “Did Abu Talhah send you?” I said: “Yes.” He said: “For food?” I said: “Yes.” He said to those with him: “Get up.” He set off, and I went ahead of them.

notes: The selected I stood there is retained, although both English comparison bodies omit it. The singular he set off and plural ahead of them remain. The historical print expands Ishaq’s lineage and reads those around him; the selected chain and those with him are preserved. The selected chapter title ends responding there (فيه), unlike the prints’ from it (منه); the Arabic heading is not silently replaced.

segments.arabic: [413] حدثنا يحيى قال: أخبرنا عبد الرزاق قال: أخبرنا ابن جريج قال: أخبرني ابن شهاب عن سهل بن سعد
segments.english: Yahya related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Razzaq informed us. He said: Ibn Jurayj informed us. He said: Ibn Shihab informed me, from Sahl ibn Sa‘d:

segments.arabic: أن رجلا قال: يا رسول الله أرأيت رجلا وجد مع امرأته رجلا أيقتله فتلاعنا في المسجد وأنا شاهد
segments.english: A man said: “Messenger of Allah, what do you think of a man who finds a man with his wife? Should he kill him?” Then the two performed li‘an in the mosque, while I was present.

notes: The unnamed man’s question remains a question, followed by the two performing lian while the narrator was present. No affirmative answer, permission to kill, accusation details, husband label or legal explanation from a comparison is inserted. Lian is retained as the technical term rather than adding the full legal procedure to the source quotation. The historical print expands Yahya to Ibn Musa and uses related-to-us for Abd al-Razzaq; the selected unexpanded name and informed-us remain.

segments.arabic: [414] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة قال: حدثنا إبراهيم بن سعد عن ابن شهاب عن محمود بن الربيع عن عتبان بن مالك
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘, from ‘Itban ibn Malik:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ أتاه في منزله، فقال أين تحب أن أصلي لك من بيتك قال: فأشرت له إلى مكان فكبر النبي ﷺ وصففنا خلفه فصلى ركعتين
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to him at his home and said: “Where in your house would you like me to pray for you?” He said: I pointed out a place to him. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said “Allah is greater,” and we formed rows behind him. He prayed two rak‘ahs.

notes: The visit, question including for you, indicated place, takbir, rows and two rakahs remain. The first third-person attribution and subsequent first-person account are retained, rather than harmonized into the comparison’s first-person opening. The fuller account at 415 is not copied here.

segments.arabic: [415] حدثنا سعيد بن عفير قال: حدثني الليث قال: حدثني عقيل عن ابن شهاب قال: أخبرني محمود بن الربيع الأنصارى
segments.english: Sa‘id ibn ‘Ufayr related to us. He said: Al-Layth related to me. He said: ‘Uqayl related to me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘ al-Ansari informed me:

segments.arabic: أن عتبان بن مالك وهو من أصحاب رسول الله ﷺ ممن شهد بدرا من الأنصار أنه أتى رسول الله ﷺ، فقال: يا رسول الله قد أنكرت بصري وأنا أصلي لقومي فإذا كانت الأمطار سال الوادي الذي بيني وبينهم لم أستطع أن آتي مسجدهم فأصلي بهم ووددت يا رسول الله أنك تأتيني فتصلي في بيتي فأتخذه مصلى قال، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: سأفعل إن شاء الله
segments.english: ‘Itban ibn Malik, who was one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and one of the Ansar who had witnessed Badr, came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said: “Messenger of Allah, my eyesight has deteriorated, and I lead my people in prayer. When the rains come, the valley between me and them flows, and I cannot reach their mosque to lead them in prayer. Messenger of Allah, I would like you to come and pray in my house so that I may take it as a place of prayer.” He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “I will do so, if Allah wills.”

segments.arabic: قال عتبان فغدا رسول الله ﷺ وأبو بكر حين ارتفع النهار فاستأذن رسول الله ﷺ فأذنت له فلم يجلس حتى دخل البيت، ثم قال أين تحب أن أصلي من بيتك قال: فأشرت له إلى ناحية من البيت فقام رسول الله ﷺ فكبر فقمنا فصففنا فصلى ركعتين ثم سلم
segments.english: ‘Itban said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr came in the morning when the day had advanced. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, asked permission to enter, and I gave him permission. He did not sit down until he had entered the house. Then he said: “Where in your house would you like me to pray?” He said: I pointed out a part of the house to him. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood and said “Allah is greater.” We stood and formed rows. He prayed two rak‘ahs, then gave the salutation.

segments.arabic: قال وحبسناه على خزيرة صنعناها له قال: فثاب في البيت رجال من أهل الدار ذوو عدد فاجتمعوا،
segments.english: He said: We kept him for some khazirah that we had prepared for him. He said: A number of men from the neighbourhood came into the house and gathered.

segments.arabic: فقال قائل منهم أين مالك بن الدخيشن أو بن الدخشن، فقال بعضهم ذلك منافق لا يحب الله ورسوله، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: لا تقل ذلك ألا تراه قد قال لا إله إلا الله يريد بذلك وجه الله قال الله ورسوله أعلم قال: فإنا نرى وجهه ونصيحته إلى المنافقين قال رسول الله ﷺ: فإن الله قد حرم على النار من قال لا إله إلا الله يبتغي بذلك وجه الله
segments.english: One of them said: “Where is Malik ibn al-Dukhayshin—or Ibn al-Dukhshun?” Some of them said: “That is a hypocrite who does not love Allah and His Messenger.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do not say that. Do you not see that he has said ‘There is no god but Allah,’ desiring by that the face of Allah?” He said: “Allah and His Messenger know best.” He said: “We see his attention and his counsel directed towards the hypocrites.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Allah has forbidden the Fire to anyone who says ‘There is no god but Allah,’ seeking by that the face of Allah.”

segments.arabic: قال ابن شهاب ثم سألت الحصين بن محمد الأنصارى وهو أحد بني سالم وهو من سراتهم عن حديث محمود بن الربيع فصدقه بذلك
segments.english: Ibn Shihab said: Then I asked al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ansari, who was one of Banu Salim and one of their leading men, about the account of Mahmud ibn al-Rabi‘, and he confirmed it.

notes: Both inspected prints read سال الوادي, the valley flowed, where the selected digital text has سأل الوادي. A declared hamzah correction follows the prints; the complete original digital paragraph remains accessible, and no other source character changes.

The complete introductory attribution, deteriorating eyesight, rain, request, if Allah wills, morning arrival, permission, location, prayer and meal remain. The selected until he had entered (حتى دخل) is retained; the historical print and English comparisons use when he entered, a documented variant. The food name khazirah is retained without a recipe. Neighbourhood renders أهل الدار following the lexical explanation, not a narrower family-only group.

Both alternatives in Malik’s name remain. The speaker who makes the accusation and replies Allah and His Messenger know best is not newly named. Face-of-Allah wording is retained in both statements, without replacing it with a theological gloss. The closing Ibn Shihab/al-Husayn confirmation remains complete as a visible transmission note, although the Khan-family EPUB omits it. The historical print differs in the initial narrator name and uses after that in the closing note; neither change is imported.

segments.arabic: [416] حدثنا سليمان بن حرب قال: حدثنا شعبة عن الأشعث بن سليم عن أبيه عن مسروق عن عائشة قالت
segments.english: Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from al-Ash‘ath ibn Sulaym, from his father, from Masruq, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ يحب التيمن ما استطاع في شأنه كله في طهوره وترجله وتنعله
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, liked to begin with the right as far as he could in all his affairs: in his purification, combing his hair and putting on his sandals.

notes: The qualifier as far as he could, all his affairs and all three examples remain. No for good things restriction from the English EPUB is added to the report. The separate Ibn Umar chapter introduction is not included in the narration script.

segments.arabic: [417] حدثنا محمد بن المثنى قال: حدثنا يحيى عن هشام قال: أخبرني أبي عن عائشة
segments.english: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from Hisham, who said: My father informed me, from ‘A’ishah:

segments.arabic: أن أم حبيبة وأم سلمة ذكرتا كنيسة رأينها بالحبشة فيها تصاوير فذكرتا للنبي ﷺ، فقال إن أولئك إذا كان فيهم الرجل الصالح فمات بنوا على قبره مسجدا وصوروا فيه تلك الصور فأولئك شرار الخلق عند الله يوم القيامة
segments.english: Umm Habibah and Umm Salamah mentioned a church they had seen in Abyssinia in which there were pictures. They mentioned it to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he said: “Those people, when a righteous man among them dies, build a place of worship over his grave and make those pictures in it. They are the worst of creation before Allah on the Day of Resurrection.”

notes: Both women, the unnamed church, pictures, righteous man, grave and Day of Resurrection remain. The church name and righteous-servant-or-man alternative from 424 are not imported. The source wording is translated as a historical report without adding contemporary application.

segments.arabic: [418] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا عبد الوارث عن أبي التياح عن أنس قال
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us, from Abu al-Tayyah, from Anas, who said:

segments.arabic: قدم النبي ﷺ المدينة فنزل أعلى المدينة في حي يقال لهم بنو عمرو بن عوف فأقام النبي ﷺ فيهم أربع عشرة ليلة ثم أرسل إلى بني النجار فجاءوا متقلدي السيوف كأني أنظر إلى النبي ﷺ على راحلته وأبو بكر ردفه وملأ بني النجار حوله حتى ألقى بفناء أبي أيوب وكان يحب أن يصلي حيث أدركته الصلاة ويصلي في مرابض الغنم
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, arrived in Madinah and stayed in the upper part of Madinah among a clan called Banu ‘Amr ibn ‘Awf. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, remained among them for fourteen nights. Then he sent for Banu al-Najjar, and they came wearing their swords. It is as though I am looking at the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on his riding camel, with Abu Bakr behind him and a gathering of Banu al-Najjar around him, until he alighted in Abu Ayyub’s courtyard. He liked to pray wherever the prayer time overtook him, and he would pray in sheepfolds.

segments.arabic: وأنه أمر ببناء المسجد فأرسل إلى ملأ من بني النجار، فقال: يا بني النجار ثامنوني بحائطكم هذا قالوا لا والله لا نطلب ثمنه إلا إلى الله،
segments.english: He ordered the mosque to be built and sent for a gathering of Banu al-Najjar. He said: “Banu al-Najjar, agree with me on a price for this walled garden of yours.” They said: “No, by Allah! We seek its price only from Allah.”

segments.arabic: فقال أنس فكان فيه ما أقول لكم قبور المشركين وفيه خرب وفيه نخل فأمر النبي ﷺ بقبور المشركين فنبشت ثم بالخرب فسويت وبالنخل فقطع فصفوا النخل قبلة المسجد وجعلوا عضادتيه الحجارة وجعلوا ينقلون الصخر وهم يرتجزون والنبي ﷺ معهم وهو يقول
segments.english: Anas said: It contained what I am telling you: graves of polytheists, ruins and date palms. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ordered the polytheists’ graves to be dug up, then the ruins to be levelled and the date palms to be cut down. They lined up the date palms at the qiblah of the mosque and made its two sides of stone. They began carrying the rocks while chanting verses. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was with them, saying:

segments.arabic: اللهم لا خير إلا خير الآخرة
segments.english: “O Allah, there is no good except the good of the Hereafter,

segments.arabic: فاغفر للأنصار والمهاجرة
segments.english: so forgive the Ansar and the Emigrants.”

notes: All three original paragraphs are retained, including both closing verse lines in source order. Fourteen nights, the upper part of Madinah, clan, swords, Abu Bakr riding behind, gathering, courtyard, sheepfolds, price request and response remain. No later purchase price, owners’ names or route date is supplied.

Ruins provisionally renders خرب; the English EPUB has uneven land, while commentary records lexical variants. Two sides provisionally renders عضادتيه; commentary also discusses doorpost/support senses. These remain lexical review items, without adding an architectural reconstruction. The selected opening O Allah, good of the Hereafter and forgive (not help) are preserved in the verse lines. The historical print adds عز وجل and another preposition before the Emigrants; neither addition replaces the selected text.

segments.arabic: [419] حدثنا سليمان بن حرب قال: حدثنا شعبة عن أبي التياح عن أنس قال:
segments.english: Sulayman ibn Harb related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from Abu al-Tayyah, from Anas, who said:

segments.arabic: كان النبي ﷺ يصلي في مرابض الغنم
segments.english: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to pray in sheepfolds.

segments.arabic: ثم سمعته بعد يقول كان يصلي في مرابض الغنم قبل أن يبنى المسجد
segments.english: Then, later, I heard him say: “He used to pray in sheepfolds before the mosque was built.”

notes: Both the initial statement and later hearing remain. The later phrase is a separate visible transmission note, with its pronouns unexpanded. The English comparisons attribute the hearing to Abu al-Tayyah; Ibn Hajar identifies Shu‘bah. The selected Arabic does not name the speaker here, so neither attribution is inserted into the translation. No narrator hearing the Prophet directly is implied.

segments.arabic: [420] حدثنا صدقة بن الفضل قال: أخبرنا سليمان بن حيان قال: حدثنا عبيد الله عن نافع قال:
segments.english: Sadaqah ibn al-Fadl related to us. He said: Sulayman ibn Hayyan informed us. He said: ‘Ubayd Allah related to us, from Nafi‘, who said:

segments.arabic: رأيت ابن عمر يصلي إلى بعيره، وقال: رأيت النبي ﷺ يفعله
segments.english: I saw Ibn ‘Umar praying towards his camel, and he said: “I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, do it.”

notes: The selected informed-us and related-to-us links remain; the historical print uses related-to-us for Sulayman. The camel-facing action is preserved without inserting sutrah, barrier or kneeling details absent from this source.

segments.arabic: [421] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة عن مالك عن زيد بن أسلم عن عطاء بن يسار عن عبد الله بن عباس قال
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Ata’ ibn Yasar, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

segments.arabic: انخسفت الشمس فصلى رسول الله ﷺ، ثم قال أريت النار فلم أر منظرا كاليوم قط أفظع
segments.english: The sun was eclipsed, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed. Then he said: “I was shown the Fire, and I have never seen a sight more terrifying than today.”

notes: The eclipse, prayer and terrifying sight remain without inserting an eclipse-prayer label, now or details from the longer account. The chain retains Abd Allah ibn Abbas. The chapter’s oven/fire context and separate displayed-Fire quotation do not enter the report.

segments.arabic: [422] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى عن عبيد الله قال: أخبرني نافع عن ابن عمر عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah, who said: Nafi‘ informed me, from Ibn ‘Umar, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: اجعلوا في بيوتكم من صلاتكم ولا تتخذوها قبورا
segments.english: “Make some of your prayer in your houses, and do not make them graves.”

notes: The complete instruction keeps some of your prayer and houses/graves without adding optional prayers or the Nawafil parenthesis from the English comparison. Juristic interpretation stays outside the source wording.

segments.arabic: [423] حدثنا إسماعيل بن عبد الله قال: حدثني مالك عن عبد الله بن دينار عن عبد الله بن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما أن رسول الله ﷺ قال
segments.english: Isma‘il ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Malik related to me, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: لا تدخلوا على هؤلاء المعذبين إلا أن تكونوا باكين فإن لم تكونوا باكين فلا تدخلوا عليهم لا يصيبكم ما أصابهم
segments.english: “Do not enter upon these people who were punished unless you are weeping. If you are not weeping, do not enter upon them, lest what befell them befall you.”

notes: The full dual honorific remains. The weeping condition, repeated entry prohibition and final lest-clause remain without adding a place name, curse or named punishment from comparison wording. The separate chapter quotation about Babylon remains browsing material.

segments.arabic: [424] حدثنا محمد قال: أخبرنا عبدة عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة
segments.english: Muhammad related to us. He said: ‘Abdah informed us, from Hisham ibn ‘Urwah, from his father, from ‘A’ishah:

segments.arabic: أن أم سلمة ذكرت لرسول الله ﷺ كنيسة رأتها بأرض الحبشة يقال لها مارية فذكرت له ما رأت فيها من الصور، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: أولئك قوم إذا مات فيهم العبد الصالح أو الرجل الصالح بنوا على قبره مسجدا وصوروا فيه تلك الصور أولئك شرار الخلق عند الله
segments.english: Umm Salamah mentioned to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, a church she had seen in the land of Abyssinia, called Mariyah. She told him about the pictures she had seen in it. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “Those are people who, when a righteous servant—or a righteous man—among them dies, build a place of worship over his grave and make those pictures in it. They are the worst of creation before Allah.”

notes: The selected Muhammad remains unexpanded; the historical print names Ibn Sallam. The church name Mariyah, both source honorifics and explicit righteous servant or righteous man alternative remain; the English EPUB compresses that alternative, and the historical print has and. No Day of Resurrection phrase is imported from 417.

segments.arabic: [425] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري أخبرني عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة أن عائشة وعبد الله بن عباس قالا
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Utbah informed me that ‘A’ishah and ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abbas said:

segments.arabic: لما نزل برسول الله ﷺ طفق يطرح خميصة له على وجهه فإذا اغتم بها كشفها عن وجهه، فقال وهو كذلك لعنة الله على اليهود والنصارى اتخذوا قبور أنبيائهم مساجد يحذر ما صنعوا
segments.english: When death came upon the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he began putting a khamisah of his over his face. When it made him feel suffocated, he uncovered his face. While in that state, he said: “Allah’s curse be upon the Jews and the Christians. They took the graves of their prophets as places of prayer.” He was warning against what they had done.

notes: The selected entry remains one complete report under an untitled chapter. The modern print assigns the combined labels 435–436 to the joint Aisha/Ibn Abbas report; no duplicate numbered entry is created. Both prints confirm the deathbed setting and warning. Khamisah is retained as the garment term. The dying state is rendered from لما نزل, not supplied as a separate quotation or contemporary application.

segments.arabic: [426] حدثنا عبد الله بن مسلمة عن مالك عن ابن شهاب عن سعيد بن المسيب عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Maslamah related to us, from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: قاتل الله اليهود اتخذوا قبور أنبيائهم مساجد
segments.english: “May Allah curse the Jews. They took the graves of their prophets as places of prayer.”

notes: The Arabic idiom قاتل الله is provisionally rendered May Allah curse, consistent with the Khan-family comparison and al-Nawawi’s lexical explanation of the same report in Muslim 530. segments.arabic: [427] حدثنا محمد بن سنان قال: حدثنا هشيم قال: حدثنا سيار هو أبو الحكم قال: حدثنا يزيد الفقير قال: حدثنا جابر بن عبد الله قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Sinan related to us. He said: Hushaym related to us. He said: Sayyar—who is Abu al-Hakam—related to us. He said: Yazid al-Faqir related to us. He said: Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: أعطيت خمسا لم يعطهن أحد من الأنبياء قبلي نصرت بالرعب مسيرة شهر وجعلت لي الأرض مسجدا وطهورا وأيما رجل من أمتي أدركته الصلاة فليصل وأحلت لي الغنائم وكان النبي يبعث إلى قومه خاصة وبعثت إلى الناس كافة وأعطيت الشفاعة
segments.english: “I have been given five things that none of the prophets before me was given. I have been aided by fear over a distance of a month’s journey. The earth has been made for me a place of prayer and a means of purification, and whichever man of my community is overtaken by the time of prayer, let him pray. The spoils have been made lawful for me. A prophet used to be sent to his own people specifically, while I have been sent to all people. I have been given intercession.”

segments.arabic: [428] حدثنا عبيد بن إسماعيل قال: حدثنا أبو أسامة عن هشام عن أبيه عن عائشة
segments.english: ‘Ubayd ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: Abu Usamah related to us, from Hisham, from his father, from ‘A’ishah:

segments.arabic: أن وليدة كانت سوداء لحي من العرب فأعتقوها فكانت معهم قالت فخرجت صبية لهم عليها وشاح أحمر من سيور قالت فوضعته أو وقع منها فمرت به حدياة وهو ملقى فحسبته لحما فخطفته قالت فالتمسوه فلم يجدوه قالت فاتهموني به قالت فطفقوا يفتشون حتى فتشوا قبلها
segments.english: A black slave woman belonged to an Arab clan. They set her free, and she stayed with them. She said: “A young girl of theirs went out wearing a red wishah made of leather strips.” She said: “She put it down, or it fell from her. A kite passed by it while it lay there, thought it was meat and snatched it.” She said: “They looked for it but did not find it.” She said: “They accused me of it.” She said: They began searching, until they even searched her private parts.

segments.arabic: قالت والله إني لقائمة معهم إذ مرت الحدياة فألقته قالت فوقع بينهم قالت فقلت: هذا الذي اتهمتموني به زعمتم وأنا منه بريئة وهو ذا هو
segments.english: She said: “By Allah, I was standing with them when the kite passed by and dropped it.” She said: “It fell among them.” She said: “I said: ‘This is what you accused me of, as you claimed, while I am innocent of it. Here it is!’”

segments.arabic: قالت فجاءت إلى رسول الله ﷺ فأسلمت قالت عائشة فكان لها خباء في المسجد أو حفش قالت فكانت تأتيني فتحدث عندي قالت فلا تجلس عندي مجلسا إلا قالت
segments.english: She said: She came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and became a Muslim. ‘A’ishah said: She had a tent in the mosque, or a small hut. She said: She used to come to me and talk with me. She said: She never sat with me without saying:

segments.arabic: ويوم الوشاح من أعاجيب ربنا
segments.english: “The day of the wishah is among the wonders of our Lord;

segments.arabic: ألا إنه من بلدة الكفر أنجاني
segments.english: indeed, He rescued me from the town of unbelief.”

segments.arabic: قالت عائشة فقلت لها ما شأنك لا تقعدين معي مقعدا إلا قلت: هذا قالت فحدثتني بهذا الحديث
segments.english: ‘A’ishah said: I said to her: “Why is it that you never sit with me without saying this?” She said: She told me this account.

notes: All four Arabic paragraphs remain, including both verse lines and the closing Aisha question and answer. The selected أعاجيب differs from تعاجيب in both prints; the selected lexical form is not silently corrected. The report keeps the put-down-or-fell and tent-or-hut uncertainties, every she-said attribution, the intervening third-person her private parts and the later return to first-person speech.

Wishah is retained as the garment/accessory term, with the selected description red and made of leather strips. No jewels, added punishment or explanatory name is imported from another comparison or parallel. The second verse line retains its pronoun He; English interpretation of the antecedent and the wishah term remains subject to independent review.

segments.arabic: [429] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا يحيى عن عبيد الله قال: حدثني نافع قال: أخبرني عبد الله
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya related to us, from ‘Ubayd Allah. He said: Nafi‘ related to me. He said: ‘Abd Allah informed me:

segments.arabic: أنه كان ينام وهو شاب أعزب لا أهل له في مسجد النبي ﷺ
segments.english: He used to sleep in the mosque of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, when he was young, unmarried and had no family.

Ibn Hajar explains the no-wife reading as repetition of unmarried and also records the broader relatives reading; the choice remains provisional.

segments.arabic: [430] حدثنا قتيبة بن سعيد قال: حدثنا عبد العزيز بن أبي حازم عن أبي حازم عن سهل بن سعد قال
segments.english: Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Abi Hazim related to us, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa‘d, who said:

segments.arabic: جاء رسول الله ﷺ بيت فاطمة فلم يجد عليا في البيت، فقال أين بن عمك قالت كان بيني وبينه شيء فغاضبني فخرج فلم يقل عندي،
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came to Fatimah’s house and did not find ‘Ali in the house. He said: “Where is your cousin?” She said: “There was something between me and him. He became angry with me and went out, and did not take his midday rest with me.”

segments.arabic: فقال رسول الله ﷺ: لإنسان انظر أين هو فجاء، فقال: يا رسول الله هو في المسجد راقد فجاء رسول الله ﷺ وهو مضطجع قد سقط رداؤه عن شقه وأصابه تراب فجعل رسول الله ﷺ يمسحه عنه ويقول قم أبا تراب قم أبا تراب
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to someone: “Look where he is.” He came and said: “Messenger of Allah, he is lying asleep in the mosque.” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came while he was lying there. His cloak had fallen from his side, and dust had settled on him. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, began wiping it off him, saying: “Get up, Abu Turab. Get up, Abu Turab.”

notes: The unnamed disagreement, cousin relationship, midday rest, search, cloak falling from his side, dust on him and both repetitions of Get up, Abu Turab remain. The name Abu Turab is not replaced by a nickname explanation inside the quote. The historical print differs at the clause about remaining with Fatimah; the selected فلم يقل and modern print support midday rest.

segments.arabic: [431] حدثنا يوسف بن عيسى قال: حدثنا ابن فضيل عن أبيه عن أبي حازم عن أبي هريرة قال:
segments.english: Yusuf ibn ‘Isa related to us. He said: Ibn Fudayl related to us, from his father, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

segments.arabic: رأيت سبعين من أصحاب الصفة ما منهم رجل عليه رداء إما إزار وإما كساء قد ربطوا في أعناقهم فمنها ما يبلغ نصف الساقين ومنها ما يبلغ الكعبين فيجمعه بيده كراهية أن ترى عورته
segments.english: I saw seventy of the people of the Suffah, none of whom had a cloak. They had either a waist-wrapper or a covering that they had tied around their necks. Some reached halfway down the shins, and some reached the ankles. Each would gather it in his hand, not wanting his private parts to be seen.

notes: Seventy, both kinds of covering, both lengths, neck fastening and the singular hand action remain. The selected companions-of-the-Suffah wording is preserved despite the modern print using people-of-the-Suffah. No garment-size or ownership explanation is added.

segments.arabic: [432] حدثنا خلاد بن يحيى قال: حدثنا مسعر قال: حدثنا محارب بن دثار عن جابر بن عبد الله قال
segments.english: Khallad ibn Yahya related to us. He said: Mis‘ar related to us. He said: Muharib ibn Dithar related to us, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, who said:

segments.arabic: أتيت النبي ﷺ وهو في المسجد
segments.english: I came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while he was in the mosque.

segments.arabic: قال مسعر أراه قال ضحى،
segments.english: Mis‘ar said: I think he said, “In the forenoon.”

segments.arabic: فقال صل ركعتين وكان لي عليه دين فقضاني وزادني
segments.english: He said: “Pray two rak‘ahs.” He owed me a debt, and he repaid me and gave me extra.

notes: Mis’ar’s uncertainty about the forenoon remains a visible transmission note between the visit and the response. It is not silently made part of Jabir’s certain statement. The full debt repayment and extra amount remain without importing the camel-sale context from a parallel.

segments.arabic: [433] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن عامر بن عبد الله بن الزبير عن عمرو بن سليم الزرقي عن أبي قتادة السلمي أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from ‘Amir ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from ‘Amr ibn Sulaym al-Zuraqi, from Abu Qatadah al-Sulami, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.english: “When one of you enters the mosque, let him pray two rak‘ahs before sitting down.”

segments.arabic: [434] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن أبي الزناد عن الأعرج عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: الملائكة تصلي على أحدكم ما دام في مصلاه الذي صلى فيه ما لم يحدث تقول اللهم اغفر له اللهم ارحمه
segments.english: “The angels pray for one of you as long as he remains in the place where he prayed, so long as he does not break his state of ritual purity. They say: ‘O Allah, forgive him. O Allah, have mercy on him.’”

segments.arabic: [435] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا يعقوب بن إبراهيم بن سعد قال: حدثني أبي عن صالح بن كيسان قال: حدثنا نافع أن عبد الله أخبره
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us. He said: My father related to me, from Salih ibn Kaysan. He said: Nafi‘ related to us that ‘Abd Allah informed him:

segments.arabic: أن المسجد كان على عهد رسول الله ﷺ مبنيا باللبن وسقفه الجريد وعمده خشب النخل فلم يزد فيه أبو بكر شيئا وزاد فيه عمر وبناه على بنيانه في عهد رسول الله ﷺ باللبن والجريد وأعاد عمده خشبا ثم غيره عثمان فزاد فيه زيادة كثيرة وبنى جداره بالحجارة المنقوشة والقصة وجعل عمده من حجارة منقوشة وسقفه بالساج
segments.english: In the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the mosque was built of mud bricks, its roof was palm fronds, and its pillars were palm wood. Abu Bakr did not add anything to it. ‘Umar added to it and built it according to its construction in the time of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with mud bricks and palm fronds, and made its pillars of wood again. Then ‘Uthman changed it, adding a great deal to it. He built its wall of carved stone and plaster, made its pillars of carved stone, and roofed it with teak.

notes: The selected unexpanded Abd Allah and all three construction stages remain. Mud bricks, palm fronds, palm wood, replacement pillars, carved stone, plaster and teak remain distinct. Plaster provisionally renders القصة; comparison terminology includes lime. The separate chapter quotations do not enter narration.

segments.arabic: [436] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا عبد العزيز بن مختار قال: حدثنا خالد الحذاء عن عكرمة
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Mukhtar related to us. He said: Khalid al-Hadhdha’ related to us, from ‘Ikrimah:

segments.arabic: قال لي ابن عباس ولابنه علي انطلقا إلى أبي سعيد فاسمعا من حديثه فانطلقنا فإذا هو في حائط يصلحه فأخذ رداءه فاحتبى ثم أنشأ يحدثنا حتى أتى ذكر بناء المسجد،
segments.english: Ibn ‘Abbas said to me and to his son ‘Ali: “Go to Abu Sa‘id and listen to some of his narrations.” We went and found him tending a walled garden. He took his cloak and sat with his knees drawn up and wrapped in it. Then he began relating to us until he came to mention the building of the mosque.

segments.arabic: فقال كنا نحمل لبنة لبنة وعمار لبنتين لبنتين فرآه النبي ﷺ فينفض التراب عنه ويقول ويح عمار تقتله الفئة الباغية يدعوهم إلى الجنة ويدعونه إلى النار قال يقول عمار أعوذ بالله من الفتن
segments.english: He said: We used to carry one brick at a time, while ‘Ammar carried two at a time. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, saw him and brushed the dust off him, saying: “Alas for ‘Ammar! The rebellious group will kill him. He calls them to Paradise, and they call him to the Fire.” He said: ‘Ammar would say: “I seek refuge in Allah from tribulations.”

notes: The whole introductory visit, cloak posture, one/two brick contrast and closing refuge statement remain. Both inspected Arabic prints explicitly contain تقتله الفئة الباغية. The selected The rebellious group will kill him is retained; the checked English EPUB omits that clause from its main quotation and supplies a parenthetical group identification instead. Bewley includes the clause.

Alas for provisionally renders the compassion expression ويح without inserting Allah into a clause where the source does not name Him. No names of later factions, battle, date or political interpretation are added. The complete Quranic chapter quotation remains separate browsing material.

segments.arabic: [437] حدثنا قتيبة قال: حدثنا عبد العزيز عن أبي حازم عن سهل قال
segments.english: Qutaybah related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz related to us, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl, who said:

segments.arabic: بعث رسول الله ﷺ إلى امرأة مري غلامك النجار يعمل لي أعوادا أجلس عليهن
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent to a woman: “Tell your carpenter slave to make me a wooden structure that I can sit on.”

notes: The selected names Qutaybah, Abd al-Aziz and Sahl remain unexpanded. Wooden structure renders أعوادا without adding pulpit to this report. The commanded carpenter-slave relationship and sitting purpose remain.

segments.arabic: [438] حدثنا خلاد قال: حدثنا عبد الواحد بن أيمن عن أبيه عن جابر
segments.english: Khallad related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid ibn Ayman related to us, from his father, from Jabir:

segments.arabic: أن امرأة قالت: يا رسول الله ألا أجعل لك شيئا تقعد عليه فإن لي غلاما نجارا قال إن شئت فعملت المنبر
segments.english: A woman said: “Messenger of Allah, shall I have something made for you to sit on? I have a slave who is a carpenter.” He said: “If you wish.” So she had the pulpit made.

notes: The conditional If you wish remains without adding the EPUB’s Yes. The woman has the pulpit made; no carpenter’s personal name, wood species or construction account from a parallel is inserted. The historical print expands Khallad’s name; the selected name remains.

segments.arabic: [439] حدثنا يحيى بن سليمان حدثني ابن وهب أخبرني عمرو أن بكيرا حدثه أن عاصم بن عمر بن قتادة حدثه أنه سمع عبيد الله الخولاني أنه سمع عثمان بن عفان يقول
segments.english: Yahya ibn Sulayman related to us. Ibn Wahb related to me. ‘Amr informed me that Bukayr related to him that ‘Asim ibn ‘Umar ibn Qatadah related to him that he heard ‘Ubayd Allah al-Khawlani, who heard ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan say:

segments.arabic: عند قول الناس فيه حين بنى مسجد الرسول ﷺ إنكم أكثرتم وإني سمعت النبي ﷺ يقول: من بنى مسجدا
segments.english: When people were speaking about him as he built the mosque of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: “You have said a great deal. I heard the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘Whoever builds a mosque’—

segments.arabic: قال بكير حسبت أنه قال يبتغي به وجه الله
segments.english: Bukayr said: I think he said, “Seeking by it the face of Allah”—

segments.arabic: بنى الله له مثله في الجنة
segments.english: ‘Allah will build its like for him in Paradise.’”

notes: The complete hearing chain and Bukayr’s uncertain seeking-the-face-of-Allah clause remain in their source order. The source does not name the person whose words Bukayr is recalling, so Asim is not inserted from the EPUB. The historical print adds an Uthman honorific and says Messenger where the selected and modern wording say Prophet; neither addition changes the selected text.

segments.arabic: [440] حدثنا قتيبة بن سعيد قال: حدثنا سفيان قال:
segments.english: Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us. He said:

segments.arabic: قلت لعمرو أسمعت جابر بن عبد الله يقول مر رجل في المسجد ومعه سهام، فقال له رسول الله ﷺ أمسك بنصالها
segments.english: I said to ‘Amr: “Did you hear Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah say: ‘A man passed through the mosque carrying arrows, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him: “Hold them by their heads”’?”

notes: Sufyan’s I said to Amr and Did you hear question are retained, rather than compressed into a direct Jabir report as in both English comparisons. Neither inspected print supplies a final Yes here. A later parallel discussed by Ibn Hajar includes Amr’s answer; that later answer is not imported into the selected report.

segments.arabic: [441] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل قال: حدثنا عبد الواحد قال: حدثنا أبو بردة بن عبد الله قال: سمعت أبا بردة عن أبيه عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahid related to us. He said: Abu Burdah ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: I heard Abu Burdah, from his father, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: من مر في شيء من مساجدنا أو أسواقنا بنبل فليأخذ على نصالها لا يعقر بكفه مسلما
segments.english: “Whoever passes through any of our mosques or markets with arrows should hold them by their heads, so that he does not injure a Muslim with his hand.”

notes: The two Abu Burdah links and from his father remain distinct in the complete chain. The final with his hand wording remains; the instruction is not detached from its stated purpose of avoiding injury.

segments.arabic: [442] حدثنا أبو اليمان الحكم بن نافع قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن بن عوف أنه سمع حسان بن ثابت الأنصارى يستشهد أبا هريرة
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman al-Hakam ibn Nafi‘ related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri. He said: Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf informed me that he heard Hassan ibn Thabit al-Ansari ask Abu Hurayrah to bear witness:

segments.arabic: أنشدك الله هل سمعت النبي ﷺ يقول: يا حسان أجب عن رسول الله ﷺ اللهم أيده بروح القدس قال أبو هريرة نعم
segments.english: “I ask you by Allah: did you hear the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘Hassan, answer on behalf of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. O Allah, support him with the Holy Spirit’?” Abu Hurayrah said: “Yes.”

notes: The complete name Abu al-Yaman al-Hakam ibn Nafi, the witness request, both Prophet/Messenger honorifics and Abu Hurayrah’s Yes remain. The Holy Spirit wording is not replaced by an inserted personal name or explanatory parenthesis.

segments.arabic: [443] حدثنا عبد العزيز بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا إبراهيم بن سعد عن صالح عن ابن شهاب قال: أخبرني عروة بن الزبير أن عائشة قالت
segments.english: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us, from Salih, from Ibn Shihab. He said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that ‘A’ishah said:

segments.arabic: لقد رأيت رسول الله ﷺ يوما على باب حجرتي والحبشة يلعبون في المسجد ورسول الله ﷺ يسترني بردائه أنظر إلى لعبهم
segments.english: One day I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, at the door of my room while the Abyssinians were playing in the mosque. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was screening me with his cloak as I watched their play.

segments.arabic: زاد إبراهيم بن المنذر حدثنا ابن وهب أخبرني يونس عن ابن شهاب عن عروة عن عائشة قالت
segments.english: Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir added: Ibn Wahb related to us. Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

segments.arabic: رأيت النبي ﷺ والحبشة يلعبون بحرابهم
segments.english: I saw the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, while the Abyssinians were playing with their spears.

notes: Both complete transmissions remain in one selected entry, even though the modern print numbers them separately as 454 and 455. The first report does not mention spears; that detail remains in the second report, where the selected Arabic places it. The EPUB compresses the added chain, which is retained here.

segments.arabic: [444] حدثنا علي بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا سفيان عن يحيى عن عمرة عن عائشة قالت
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from Yahya, from ‘Amrah, from ‘A’ishah, who said:

segments.arabic: أتتها بريرة تسألها في كتابتها فقالت إن شئت أعطيت أهلك ويكون الولاء لي، وقال أهلها إن شئت أعطيتها ما بقي،
segments.english: Barirah came to her asking for help with her contract of emancipation. She said: “If you wish, I will pay your owners, and the wala’ will belong to me.” Her owners said: “If you wish, you can give her what remains.”

segments.arabic: وقال سفيان مرة إن شئت أعتقتها ويكون الولاء لنا
segments.english: Sufyan once said: “If you wish, you can set her free, and the wala’ will belong to us.”

segments.arabic: فلما جاء رسول الله ﷺ ذكرته ذلك، فقال ابتاعيها فأعتقيها فإن الولاء لمن أعتق ثم قام رسول الله ﷺ على المنبر،
segments.english: When the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came, I mentioned that to him. He said: “Buy her and set her free, for the wala’ belongs to the one who sets free.” Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood on the pulpit.

segments.arabic: وقال سفيان مرة فصعد رسول الله ﷺ على المنبر،
segments.english: Sufyan once said: “The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, ascended the pulpit.”

segments.arabic: فقال: ما بال أقوام يشترطون شروطا ليست في كتاب الله من اشترط شرطا ليس في كتاب الله فليس له وإن اشترط مائة مرة
segments.english: He said: “What is the matter with people who stipulate conditions that are not in the Book of Allah? Whoever stipulates a condition that is not in the Book of Allah has no right to it, even if he stipulates it a hundred times.”

segments.arabic: قال علي قال يحيى وعبد الوهاب عن يحيى عن عمرة، وقال جعفر بن عون عن يحيى قال: سمعت عمرة قالت سمعت عائشة رواه مالك عن يحيى عن عمرة أن بريرة ولم يذكر صعد المنبر
segments.english: ‘Ali said: Yahya and ‘Abd al-Wahhab said, from Yahya, from ‘Amrah. Ja‘far ibn ‘Awn said, from Yahya: “I heard ‘Amrah say: ‘I heard ‘A’ishah.’” Malik related it from Yahya, from ‘Amrah: “That Barirah…” He did not mention “ascended the pulpit.”

notes: Both Sufyan once-said variants and the complete closing Ali/Yahya/Abd al-Wahhab, Ja’far and Malik transmissions remain in source order. The historical print places the Malik note before Ali’s note and includes extra wording after Amrah; the modern print follows the selected order and shorter Ali note. No missing text is invented for the selected abbreviated closing attributions.

The selected third-person opening and later first-person I mentioned are retained. Wala’ remains the technical term rather than being reduced to inheritance alone. The who sets free wording follows the Arabic لمن أعتق; the checked EPUB incorrectly says the manumitted. The complete condition statement retains a hundred times, not an inserted a hundred conditions. No legal ruling is supplied outside the source report.

segments.arabic: [445] حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد قال: حدثنا عثمان بن عمر قال: أخبرنا يونس عن الزهري عن عبد الله بن كعب بن مالك عن كعب
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad related to us. He said: ‘Uthman ibn ‘Umar related to us. He said: Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ka‘b ibn Malik, from Ka‘b:

segments.arabic: أنه تقاضى بن أبي حدرد دينا كان له عليه في المسجد فارتفعت أصواتهما حتى سمعها رسول الله ﷺ وهو في بيته فخرج إليهما حتى كشف سجف حجرته فنادى يا كعب قال لبيك يا رسول الله قال ضع من دينك هذا وأومأ إليه أي الشطر قال لقد فعلت يا رسول الله قال قم فاقضه
segments.english: He asked Ibn Abi Hadrad in the mosque to repay a debt he owed him. Their voices rose until the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, heard them while he was in his house. He came out to them and drew aside the curtain of his room. He called out: “Ka‘b!” He said: “At your service, Messenger of Allah.” He said: “Reduce this debt of yours by this much,” and gestured to him, meaning half. He said: “I have done so, Messenger of Allah.” He said: “Get up and repay him.”

notes: The complete debt request, raised voices, curtain, named call, response, half gesture and closing repayment command remain. The selected third-person narration and unnamed closing addressee are not expanded using the EPUB’s explanatory parentheses. The modern print number is 457, illustrating why numbers are matched individually rather than by a fixed offset.
